Complete worked framework

From expert judgements to final priorities

This area brings together the full source hierarchy, the meaning of every dimension and subcriterion, the AHP calculation steps, the consistency test and the expert-derived result when survey data have been supplied.

No aggregated expert-results file is embedded in this deployment. The complete framework and method are shown below; weights remain explicitly unavailable until the owner imports valid survey responses.
1

Pairwise judgement

Experts compare two elements at a time on the 1–9 Saaty scale. Selecting A means A is more important; selecting B records the reciprocal judgement for A relative to B.

2

Consistency check

For a matrix of order n, CI = (λmax − n)/(n − 1) and CR = CI/RI. A completed matrix is retained when CR ≤ 0.10.

3

Group aggregation

Accepted individual judgements are combined pair by pair using the geometric mean, preserving the reciprocal structure of the AHP matrix.

4

Final priorities

Local subcriterion weights are multiplied by their dimension weight. These global weights allow all 27 subcriteria to be ranked on one scale.

How to interpret the worked output

Dimension weight
The share of overall sustainability importance assigned to one of the six domains.
Local weight
The priority of a subcriterion within its own dimension; local weights within each dimension sum to 1.
Global weight
Dimension weight × local weight. Global weights across all 27 subcriteria sum to 1 when every module is complete.
Missing-data flag
A weight is withheld when no valid comparison exists for one or more pairs. Missing values are never silently imputed.
